key_features: Small lesion with a regular pigment network fading at the periphery and a darker eccentric central blotch, mild asymmetry but no regression, blue-white veil, or atypical vessels, favoring a dysplastic/junctional nevus.

A pink, largely pigment-free lesion with scale, fine dotted and short linear vessels, and white structureless scar-like areas, with no pigment network; this fits an inflammatory lesion or superficial BCC, but amelanotic melanoma cannot be excluded.

A light-brown, fairly uniform pseudonetwork around regularly spaced follicular openings with fading borders suggests a solar lentigo, but the ill-defined edges and fine peripheral brown dots on what appears to be chronically sun-damaged facial skin leave lentigo maligna a real possibility.

Pink cobblestone-like lobular pattern of skin-colored globules with fine comma/linear vessels and scattered small brown dots between lobules, lacking an atypical network or blue-white veil, suggests a benign dermal or papillomatous nevus.

Large irregular lesion on sun-damaged skin with asymmetric brown dots/globules, central regression with blue-gray peppering and white scar-like areas, and irregular pigment network, suggestive of lentigo maligna/melanoma in situ; surgical margin markings visible.

Small, fairly symmetric lesion with a regular globular pattern and a darker brown-gray center fading evenly to the periphery, most consistent with a compound nevus; the gray center and mildly irregular outline keep some residual concern.

A central orange-yellow serous crust or erosion sits on diffusely pink, scaly skin with no pigment network, globules, streaks or blue-white structures, which favours an inflammatory or keratinocytic process (e.g., eroded keratosis or ulcerated lesion) over melanoma.

Symmetric oval brown lesion with uniform color, a regular rim of peripheral globules (typical of a growing Clark/Reed-type nevus), and a slightly darker homogeneous center without atypical network, regression, or blue-white veil.

An asymmetric, ill-defined brown lesion on sun-damaged skin, with uneven pigment, central regression-like whitish areas and grayish granular dots (peppering), suggests a melanocytic lesion such as lentigo maligna or melanoma.
The lesion is asymmetric and multicolored, with a central blue-gray, veil-like area and white structureless foci, an irregular brown peripheral network, and a pink rim of dotted vessels.

An asymmetric, irregularly bordered light-to-dark brown macule on sun-damaged skin, with irregular dots and globules and a central whitish regression-like area, suggesting early melanoma or lentigo maligna over a solar lentigo or lichen planus-like keratosis.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular, blurred borders, multiple colors (dark brown, light brown, blue-gray/violaceous areas), eccentric dark blotch, and regression-like gray-white zones.
Large asymmetric lesion with blue-white veil, multiple colors (blue-gray, brown, pink), irregular peripheral brown pigmentation, dotted vessels, and regression-like white areas.
Asymmetric lesion with an atypical, irregular pigment network at the periphery, a central pink-white regression area with blue-gray peppering, and irregular brown streaks/projections at the margins.
Small central light-brown delicate network patch surrounded by a white scar-like area with peripheral scaling and pinkish background, consistent with a dermatofibroma rather than melanoma.

Large asymmetric pink-tan lesion with irregular, eccentric brown pigmentation, focal blue-gray and whitish regression-like areas, and dotted/linear irregular vessels on a pink background suggest early or hypomelanotic melanoma rather than a simple nevus.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light and dark brown, eccentric blue-black blotch), irregular scalloped borders, regression-like pinkish-white areas, and atypical dotted vessels suggest melanoma.
Multiple colors (brown, blue-gray, red, white) with an extensive white scar-like regression area, blue-white veil, irregular peppering/blotches, and asymmetric structure favor melanoma.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular, ragged borders, multiple colors (brown, red-pink, blue-gray), central regression-like white areas, irregular peripheral dots/globules and atypical vessels on sun-damaged skin.

An ill-defined, asymmetric light-to-dark brown lesion with an irregular, broken atypical network, eccentric darker blotches, scattered white regression-like areas and fine red vessels, suggesting possible melanoma (e.g., in situ on sun-damaged skin), though a regressing benign lesion cannot be excluded.

Small lesion with a darker brown center and a lighter periphery of fragmented reticular pigment and dots, mildly irregular edges, no blue-white veil or atypical vessels, most consistent with a dysplastic or junctional nevus, though the patchy irregular border keeps some suspicion.

Large, ill-defined, asymmetric light-to-dark brown macule on sun-damaged skin with irregular pigment distribution, a focal blue-gray/dark area, and atypical vessels, suggestive of lentigo maligna/melanoma in situ.

Ill-defined pink erythematous patch with evenly distributed dotted vessels, no pigment network, streaks, or atypical pigmentation, which favors an inflammatory or non-melanocytic lesion, though amelanotic melanoma cannot be fully excluded.
Asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (dark brown, black, blue-gray), a blue-white veil-like area, irregular peripheral dots/globules, and irregular blotches suggest melanoma.
Large (>2 cm) asymmetric lesion with irregular notched borders, eccentric dark peripheral blotches, a faint atypical network, and central regression with white scar-like areas and grey peppering.

Asymmetric, irregularly bordered lesion with multiple colors (dark blue-black, brown, light tan), irregular dark globules/dots, an atypical pigment network, and blue-gray areas, all on sun-damaged skin, which suggests melanoma.

Small oval brown macule with a fine, fairly regular reticular network, mild color variation (olive-brown to reddish-brown) and slightly eccentric pigmentation, but no atypical network, regression, blue-white veil or irregular dots/streaks, favoring a benign (dysplastic/junctional) nevus.

Large lesion with an atypical, irregular pigment network, extensive white scar-like regression areas, peppering/granularity, pinkish areas with irregular vessels, and asymmetric multicomponent structure, all suggesting melanoma.

Large lesion with an extensive blue-white veil and blue-gray structureless areas, irregular brown-gray blotches and dots, and a reddish-brown peripheral rim with multiple colors and asymmetry, which favor invasive melanoma.

Large, ill-defined pink lesion with extensive white structureless/scar-like regression, polymorphous dotted and linear vessels, and asymmetric peripheral dark brown-black blotches and irregular dots, together suggesting regressing melanoma (possibly amelanotic) rather than a benign lesion.

The lesion is asymmetric with multiple colors (light and dark brown, violaceous-purple centrally, pink-red areas), irregular clustered dots and globules, and an eccentric, poorly defined light-brown extension with an irregular border.

An asymmetric lesion with an irregular, eccentric brown network at the periphery, a central whitish scar-like area suggesting regression, uneven dark blotches at the lower edge, and an irregular border.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light and dark brown, blue-gray, pink), blue-white veil and regression areas, irregular dots/globules, and atypical network with irregular borders, all strongly suggesting melanoma.

Light-brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with surrounding solar lentigines and a small central dark-brown focus with scale/crust; the overall pattern favors a benign lentigo or irritated nevus, but the eccentric dark spot and irregular pigmentation keep lentigo maligna in the differential.

Large, poorly defined lesion with irregular brown pigmentation, blue-gray areas, white scar-like regression structures and polymorphous dotted/pinpoint vessels on a pink background, suggesting regressing or hypomelanotic melanoma.

Large, asymmetric light-brown lesion with irregular, fragmented borders, an atypical broken network, irregular peripheral dots and globules, eccentric dark blotches, and areas of regression, suggesting melanoma in situ or lentigo maligna type.

Ill-defined pigmented macule on sun-damaged facial skin with asymmetric peppering/granularity, blue-gray dots and areas, and perifollicular annular-granular pigmentation suggestive of lentigo maligna.

A large asymmetric lesion with an irregular, blurred border, an atypical pigment network of uneven thickness, and multifocal eccentric dark blotches around central lighter, regression-like areas, a pattern suspicious for early or in-situ melanoma rather than a dysplastic nevus.
Large asymmetric lesion with irregular, notched borders, an atypical pigment network, eccentric dark blotches with multiple shades of brown, and regression-like whitish areas.

Asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light and dark brown, blue-gray/violet), an eccentric blue-gray area with peppering/granular dots, irregular borders and surrounding erythema raise concern for melanoma.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (brown, dark brown, gray-blue, pink), central regression-like pinkish-white area with dotted/linear irregular vessels, eccentric dark blotches and irregular peripheral pigmentation with gray dots.

A pink-red nodule shows polymorphous vessels (serpentine, corkscrew and glomerular-like) on a milky-red background, next to an irregular blue-gray pigmented area, which suggests amelanotic or nodular melanoma.

An asymmetric, irregularly shaped brown lesion on sun-damaged hair-bearing skin, with uneven pigment, gray-blue peppered dots centrally and a faint, poorly defined periphery, raising concern for lentigo maligna-type melanoma.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (black, dark brown, reddish-brown, blue-white veil), atypical irregular network with peripheral streaks/pseudopods, irregular dots/globules, and regression-like pink areas.

Ill-defined, asymmetric lesion on sun-damaged skin with irregular brown-pink-red coloration, blue-gray areas and dots, atypical vessels, and regression-like whitish zones, suggestive of melanoma (possibly in situ or lentigo maligna type).

A small lesion with a fairly symmetric globular-to-reticular pattern of brown globules and a darker central hyperpigmented area, but no blue-white veil, irregular streaks or atypical vessels, favoring a benign compound nevus.

An ill-defined, asymmetric light-to-dark brown macule with irregular blotches and blue-gray, regression-like structureless areas sits on sun-damaged skin with prominent vessels, which raises concern for melanoma (possibly lentigo maligna type), though the vessels could also suggest a basal cell carcinoma.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (brown, dark purple, blue-gray), a central blue-white veil, irregular peripheral dots/globules and regression-like whitish areas.

Small, poorly defined lesion on sun-damaged skin with a focal dark-brown eccentric blotch, a pinkish-red area with fine vessels and faint light-brown pigmentation; it is small and mostly featureless, but the eccentric blotch and vascular component keep melanoma, including amelanotic or in situ types, on the differential.

A large, asymmetric lesion with extensive central pinkish-white regression, irregular eccentric brown-gray blotches and dots at the periphery, focal blue-gray areas, and an atypical patchy network, suggesting melanoma with regression over a dermatofibroma-like pattern.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (light and dark brown, reddish-violet), a central blue-white veil/regression-like area, and irregular dark blotches/dots.

Small brown lesion with a fairly regular reticular/globular pigment network and an eccentric pinkish hypopigmented area with mild asymmetry, most consistent with a dysplastic/compound nevus but with some atypical features.

Small, fairly symmetric lesion with a regular pigment network that fades gradually at the periphery and a darker center, consistent with a benign nevus, though the slight irregular network extensions keep this from being a confident call.

Large, asymmetric, ill-defined light-brown lesion with irregular darker central gray-brown areas, regression-like whitish zones, blue-gray peppering, and polymorphous/dotted vessels suggest early (in situ) melanoma.

Light-to-medium brown lesion with irregular, elongated shape, two-toned pigmentation (darker brown upper portion, lighter tan reticular lower portion) and faint blurred borders, but no atypical network, regression structures, blue-white veil or atypical vessels, favoring a benign (possibly dysplastic) nevus.
Asymmetric brown lesion with irregular borders, eccentric blue-gray/black dots and blotchy areas centrally, and multiple colors with an atypical network suggest melanoma over a dysplastic nevus.

An asymmetric, irregularly star-shaped brown lesion with an uneven network, scattered blue-gray dots (peppering), whitish regression-like areas and a faded edge on sun-damaged skin together favour early melanoma.

An asymmetric, two-component lesion with structureless tan-brown lobes next to a pink amelanotic area showing polymorphous, irregular linear and dotted vessels, raising concern for a partially amelanotic melanoma.

An asymmetric, irregularly bordered lesion with an atypical, uneven pigment network, eccentric dark-brown blotches and a focal blue-gray area, suggesting melanoma (possibly in situ) over a dysplastic nevus.
Large asymmetric lesion with irregular notched borders, multiple browns to black, atypical broadened network, irregular dots and blotches, and central blue-gray veil/regression structures.

Light brown lesion with a regular, delicate pigment network and multifocal symmetric hyperpigmented blotches that fade gradually at the periphery, with no atypical structures, regression, or blue-white veil, consistent with a benign (possibly dysplastic) nevus.

Large asymmetric irregular brown lesion with a central regression-like whitish area, blue-gray peppering/granules, irregular blotchy pigmentation and an ill-defined border with a satellite pigmented focus, suggestive of melanoma in situ/early melanoma on sun-damaged skin.
Asymmetric multicomponent lesion with irregular eccentric dark brown blotches, blue-gray veil/regression-like areas, irregularly distributed dots and globules, and ill-defined uneven borders.

Small, fairly symmetric brown lesion with a regular reticular network, uniform tan-brown color, and smooth fading borders, lacking atypical structures such as blue-white veil, irregular dots, or regression; most consistent with a benign nevus.

Pink lesion on sun-damaged skin with an irregular, asymmetric blue-gray and brown pigment network, white shiny structures, regression-like areas and polymorphous vessels, suggesting melanoma (possibly lentigo maligna type), though basal cell carcinoma is a differential.
Large, highly asymmetric multicomponent lesion with irregular streaks/pseudopods, peripheral dots, blue-white veil, central scar-like regression with pink-white areas, and polymorphous vessels.

Small, fairly well-circumscribed brown lesion with mild asymmetry, darker eccentric blotches and a few bluish-gray dots, but no definite atypical network, regression, or streaks, favoring an atypical/dysplastic nevus over melanoma.

An asymmetric, irregularly notched light-brown macule with uneven pigmentation, scattered irregular brown dots and granules, and paler regression-like central areas, raising concern for melanoma in situ despite the low overall contrast.
Large asymmetric lesion with irregular notched borders, multiple colors (brown, pink, blue-gray), regression structures with gray peppering, irregular dots/globules and white scar-like areas.

Large, poorly circumscribed light-brown lesion with an irregular, fragmented network, gray-blue peppering (regression), pinkish areas and whitish structureless zones, suggesting melanoma in situ/regressing melanoma on sun-damaged skin.

Small, fairly symmetric light-brown macule with uniform reticular-to-structureless pigmentation, a soft fading border, and a few milia-like dots, with no atypical network, regression, or blue-white structures, consistent with a benign nevus.

Irregular, asymmetric brown pigmented patch on chronically sun-damaged skin with blue-gray areas, regression-like zones, irregular borders and surgical-margin ink markings, suggestive of lentigo maligna/melanoma in situ.

Large lesion with multiple colors (red-brown, dark brown, blue-gray), white scar-like regression areas, dotted/polymorphous vessels, and irregular asymmetric pigmentation extending beyond the field of view.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular, notched borders, a peripheral pigment network that is atypical and broadened in places, and an eccentric darker central area showing blue-gray structures and irregular dots, all of which raise concern for melanoma.

The lesion is an asymmetric, ill-defined light-brown to pink macule with an irregular, patchy pigment network, focal gray-blue granular peppering and whitish regression-like areas, suggesting early melanoma or melanoma in situ.

An exophytic, papillomatous lesion with a regular cobblestone pattern of large rounded globules, terminal hairs, and a fairly symmetric, evenly brown periphery suggests a congenital or dermal nevus, though its size and the pinkish nodular centre leave some uncertainty.
Ill-defined, asymmetric faint lesion with a central pink, regression-like zone containing dotted and irregular vessels, an eccentric darker brown blotch, and patchy peripheral light-brown pigment.

A large, faint, ill-defined light-brown lesion on sun-damaged skin shows asymmetric, multifocal pigmentation and fine gray-brown granular dots centrally, which raises concern for lentigo maligna, though a solar lentigo or regressing keratosis remains a real possibility.

A large, ill-defined light-brown lesion fills the field, with multifocal asymmetric blotches, an irregular, fragmented network, and pale regression-like areas on sun-damaged skin, which raises concern for melanoma in situ, though a solar lentigo or benign nevus remains possible.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular notched borders, multiple brown shades, and dark eccentric blotches plus a central blue-white veil/regression area, all concerning for melanoma.
The lesion is asymmetric, with an irregular, broken pigment network, two eccentric dark blotches, scattered irregular dots and globules, and a central whitish, regression-like structureless area.
Small but asymmetric, irregularly shaped lesion with multiple colors (brown, pink, blue-gray), a blue-white/gray veil-like central area, and irregular peripheral pigmentation on sun-damaged skin.

The lesion is asymmetric with irregular borders and mixed colors (tan-brown periphery, a central pink-violaceous zone and a whitish veil-like regression area), with no regular network, which leans toward melanoma.

Asymmetric pigmented lesion on sun-damaged skin with an irregular, atypical pigment network, an eccentric blue-gray veil-like area, and scattered irregular dark dots, all of which raise concern for melanoma.

Large, chaotic lesion with multiple colors, irregular brown blotches and atypical network, extensive white scar-like regression areas, peppering, and pink zones with polymorphous dotted vessels suggest melanoma.

Large, poorly defined lesion with multicomponent asymmetric pattern: irregular brown blotches and fragmented network at the periphery, pinkish-red regression/erythematous areas, white scar-like zones and dotted/polymorphous vessels, suggesting melanoma (possibly lentigo maligna type on sun-damaged skin).

A fairly symmetric oval brown lesion with a regular reticular-globular pattern, a lighter central area and gradual peripheral fading, partly obscured by dense hair, suggests a benign nevus, though focal darker blotches and possible bluish-gray areas keep some suspicion.

Small, fairly symmetric oval lesion with uniform reddish-brown color, a fine regular network fading gradually at the periphery, and no blue-white veil, regression structures, or atypical dots, consistent with a benign nevus on freckled skin.

A large, ill-defined, asymmetric patch with multifocal light-to-dark brown pigmentation, extensive white regression-like areas, and central gray-blue granular peppering suggests a regressing or in-situ melanoma rather than a benign nevus.

A large asymmetric lesion with an irregular, notched outline and multiple shades of brown, an atypical network thickening at the periphery, and a central darker zone with pinkish-gray regression-like areas, which favors early melanoma over a dysplastic nevus.

Large, poorly defined light-brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with an atypical, irregular network, regression-like white areas, blue-gray granular peppering, and asymmetric darker brown blotches suggest lentigo maligna/melanoma, though a biopsy is the only way to confirm.
Large asymmetric lesion with irregular, notched borders, multiple shades of brown to black, and irregularly distributed dark dots and globules with blotches and peripheral extensions.

Small, fairly symmetric, sharply demarcated dark brown-black lesion with a mostly homogeneous center and only subtle irregular pigment at the edges, most consistent with a pigmented (possibly Reed/Spitz-type or dysplastic) nevus, though the dark pigmentation and mild border irregularity keep melanoma risk moderate.

Oval, fairly symmetric brown lesion with a globular/cobblestone pattern at the periphery and a darker but uniform center, no regression, blue-white veil or atypical vessels, consistent with a growing benign nevus, though the eccentric dark center with a few dots lends mild concern.

An asymmetric lesion on sun-damaged skin shows an eccentric dark brown-black blotch with irregular, ragged borders, a contiguous light-brown extension, multiple colors and possible central blue-gray areas.
Large asymmetric lesion with blue-white veil, irregular blue-gray peppering/regression, multiple colors (pink, brown, blue, white), ulceration/scale, and polymorphous vessels on sun-damaged skin.

Facial skin showing a pink, strawberry-like background with prominent white-haloed follicular openings and fine vessels, plus a small central light-brown blotch without clear asymmetric perifollicular pigmentation, rhomboidal structures or gray dots, favoring a pigmented actinic keratosis or lentigo over lentigo maligna.

Large lesion with an atypical, irregular pigment network, regression-like white and pink areas with peppering, gray-violet dots, and asymmetric multifocal pigmentation, suggesting melanoma (possibly in situ).

Large, poorly defined, asymmetric light-tan macule with patchy, irregular pigment distribution, pinkish areas suggesting possible regression, and faint grayish-brown dots on what appears to be sun-damaged skin, raising concern for melanoma in situ (lentigo maligna type) over solar lentigo.

A large, ill-defined light-brown patch on sun-damaged skin with asymmetric, multifocal blotchy pigmentation, irregular fading borders, pink-white regression-like areas and fine vessels, which together suggest lentigo maligna.

A large, ill-defined, asymmetric light-brown lesion with multifocal patchy pigmentation, eccentric irregular dark dots and globules, and pinkish structureless areas suggesting regression, which together are concerning for early melanoma in situ.
Large asymmetric lesion extending beyond the frame, with multiple colors (dark red-brown, black, pink), a central blue-white veil/regression area, irregular blotches and poorly defined borders.

The lesion is large and markedly asymmetric with an irregular outline, an atypical, fragmented pigment network that is darker and denser in eccentric areas, and central whitish-pink regression-like zones, which together suggest a melanoma, possibly in situ.

Asymmetric pigmentation with an eccentric dark brown irregular network and globules on one side, plus a pink structureless area with polymorphous serpentine and dotted vessels, raising concern for melanoma.

Small (~6 mm) lesion with a fairly regular brown pigment network, a central darker reddish-brown homogeneous area, and mild asymmetry but no blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels, favoring a dysplastic or compound nevus over melanoma.
Asymmetric, irregularly lobulated lesion with multiple colors (orange-brown, dark brown, blue-gray), eccentric dark blotches, regression-like areas, and irregular peripheral globules/streaks.

An asymmetric, irregularly bordered lesion with several colors (light brown, reddish-brown, dark brown), irregular peripheral dark dots and globules, an off-center dark blotch, and surrounding pinkish erythema.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular, lobulated borders, multiple colors (dark brown, light brown, pink-red erythematous area), structureless pink zone suggesting regression, and central blue-white/shiny structures.

A small, ill-defined light-brown macule with a slightly darker center and a uniform tan color, showing no atypical network, regression structures, or irregular vessels, suggests a benign nevus or lentigo; the image is under a fluid-filled dome, so detail is limited.

Asymmetric, irregular light-to-dark brown blotches with granular peppering and whitish regression-like areas on sun-damaged skin with a fine vascular network raise concern for lentigo maligna, though a benign keratosis or lentigo is also possible.

A faint, poorly defined, asymmetric light-brown patch with irregular pigment distribution and whitish regression-like areas sits on sun-damaged skin with surgical ink marks, which raises concern for lentigo maligna or early melanoma.

Fairly symmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with a regular, fading reticular network, central hypopigmentation/whitish lines and no blue-white veil or atypical vessels, most consistent with a dysplastic/compound nevus; the central white lines and a slightly irregular edge keep a modest melanoma risk.

Large asymmetric multinodular lesion with pink-white regression/structureless areas, polymorphous vessels, an irregular blue-black blotch, and an irregular flat pigmented component with streaks extending at the periphery, suggesting invasive melanoma arising from an in-situ portion.

A small, ill-defined pink-tan macule with asymmetric central gray-brown granular dots (peppering) and no organized network suggests regression and makes melanoma a real possibility, though the faint, featureless pattern leaves the call uncertain.

A large, asymmetric light-to-dark brown lesion with a multifocal, irregular network, regression-like whitish and pink areas, scattered peppering and grayish dots, and poorly defined borders, suggesting melanoma (possibly in situ) on sun-damaged skin.

Elongated brown lesion with a mostly regular reticular network that fades gradually at the edges, a few eccentric darker blotches and central hypopigmentation, but no blue-white veil, regression structures or atypical vessels, favoring a (possibly dysplastic) nevus.

Small (~3-4 mm), ill-defined light-to-medium brown macule with a slightly darker violaceous-brown center and faint, fairly uniform pigment on sun-damaged freckled skin, without atypical network, streaks, regression or blue-white veil, favoring a benign nevus or lentigo.

Small brown lesion with a fairly regular reticular/globular pattern, homogeneous light-to-medium brown color, and gradual peripheral fading without blue-white veil, atypical streaks, or regression, consistent with a benign nevus.

Light tan-brown lesion with a fairly regular, symmetric reticular network that fades gradually at the periphery, with no blue-white veil, atypical dots or streaks, though there is mild pinkish erythema and slight color variation.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light and dark brown, red, blue-gray), irregular blotches, regression-like white-pink areas with blue-gray peppering, and an irregular, poorly defined border.

An asymmetric, multicomponent brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with surrounding lentigines, showing an irregular, fragmented pigment network, uneven pigmentation, and a darker eccentric lower area with irregular structures.

Asymmetric, irregularly lobulated brown lesion with an atypical pigment network, whitish-bluish regression areas, focal blue-gray peppering/granular dots inferiorly, and uneven color distribution, which together favor early melanoma over a benign nevus.

Small, fairly symmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with central hyperpigmentation fading gradually at the periphery, homogeneous/faint reticular pattern, and no atypical network, regression structures, or blue-white veil, most consistent with a benign nevus.

A light-brown lesion with peripheral globules at the rim, a fairly symmetric shape and a small central bluish-gray area, a pattern most consistent with a growing (Clark/Spitz-type) nevus, though the central blue-gray focus keeps melanoma risk non-trivial.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light and dark brown, blue-gray), central blue-white veil and regression structures, peppering/irregular dots, and an irregular network toward the periphery.

Small, symmetric light-to-dark brown lesion with a central hypopigmented area and fine peripheral pigment network or star-like projections within a perifollicular pale halo, most consistent with a dermatofibroma or a benign nevus, with no atypical blue-white structures.

A faint, ill-defined pink-tan patch with fine scale, patchy brown dots and globules concentrated toward one pole, and a pinkish background suggesting regression or inflammation; the asymmetric, focal pigment raises some concern, but the overall picture is more consistent with a benign keratosis-like or inflamed lesion.

Small, fairly symmetric brown lesion with a regular pigment network fading at the periphery and a central darker hyperpigmented area with slight blue-gray tint, most consistent with a dysplastic or junctional nevus, though the central blue-gray area keeps melanoma from being excluded.

Small pink hypomelanotic lesion on sun-damaged skin showing polymorphous dotted and linear vessels, shiny white streaks, and an eccentric brown blotch, which raises concern for melanoma over dermatofibroma or BCC.

Large asymmetric lesion with blue-gray veil and whitish areas, irregular brown-black blotches and dots at an uneven periphery, and multiple colors, all concerning for melanoma despite the follicular openings.

Blurry, low-contrast pinkish-tan field with diffuse light-brown streaky pigmentation, faint dotted vessels and immersion-fluid bubbles, without a defined atypical network, blue-white veil or irregular dots and globules, favors a benign or nonmelanocytic lesion, though the poor image quality limits confidence.

Small light-brown lesion with blurred structureless center and peripheral dots, globules and short streaks clustered asymmetrically at the left and lower edges rather than as a symmetric rim, a concerning pattern.

Asymmetric brown lesion about 8 mm across with irregular, blurred borders, central blue-gray peppering suggesting regression, and an uneven pigment network, which together favor an early melanoma over a benign nevus.

Asymmetric, ill-defined pinkish-tan lesion with irregular eccentric brown blotches, a separate pigmented focus at the top, and dotted/polymorphous vessels on a background of sun-damaged skin, which raises concern for an early or amelanotic-leaning melanoma; a benign lesion is still possible.

An asymmetric dark lesion with a blue-gray, veil-like center and irregular reddish-brown peripheral blotches outweighs the scattered milia-like white dots that would otherwise favor a seborrheic keratosis.

Fairly regular brown pigment network that thins out toward the periphery, with a darker central hyperpigmented area, mild asymmetry and an irregular outline but no regression, blue-white veil or atypical vessels, which favours a dysplastic or Clark nevus.

Light-to-medium brown lesion with a fairly regular pigment network that fades evenly at the periphery and a slightly darker center, mild asymmetry, and no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels, most consistent with a benign nevus.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (dark brown-black, light brown, blue-gray), an irregular eccentric dark blotch, atypical network, irregular dots/globules and scattered satellite-like extensions with irregular borders.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (brown, blue-gray, pink-white), blue-white veil, regression structures, irregular blotches and peripheral patchy pigmentation, plus a central pink area with atypical vessels.

Small brown lesion with a fairly regular reticular/globular network, mild asymmetry with a lighter tan extension inferiorly, no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels, favoring a benign nevus over melanoma.

Facial skin showing asymmetric, irregular brown-gray pigmentation around follicular openings with gray dots and granules (annular-granular pattern), early rhomboidal structures, and whitish regression areas, suggestive of lentigo maligna.

Small brown lesion with a fairly regular reticular-globular pattern, a darker center fading symmetrically to the periphery, a few small grey dots, and no blue-white veil or atypical vessels, which together suggest a benign nevus.
Asymmetric, irregularly bordered light-to-dark brown macule with central gray-blue areas and pigment around follicular openings, on sun-damaged skin with telangiectasias, suggests lentigo maligna.

A fairly symmetric brown lesion with a darker reticular center and a lighter brown periphery, a central hypopigmented area, a pigment network that fades evenly at the edge, and a few dots, all consistent with a dysplastic or compound nevus, though the mild asymmetry and central regression-like area leave some concern.
Large asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple brown shades, atypical network, blue-gray dots/regression areas, white scar-like zones, and a red vascular focus.

Small, fairly symmetric lesion with regular borders and a cobblestone/globular pattern of brown to bluish globules, most consistent with a benign (possibly congenital or dermal) nevus, though the blue-gray areas leave some uncertainty.

The lesion is asymmetric with an irregular, notched outline, and shows an atypical, thickened, branching pigment network that is darker and off-centre on one side, plus structureless brown and pinkish regression-like areas.
An asymmetric, lobulated lesion with irregular notched borders, a central blue-gray and whitish regression-like area, and irregular dark dots and granularity (peppering) over uneven brown pigment.

Asymmetric lesion with an eccentric, sharply demarcated brown network-like area on one side contrasting with a structureless pinkish-brown zone containing blue-gray regression areas and a whitish veil, giving multiple colors and an irregular structural pattern.

Irregular, asymmetric light-brown pigmentation on sun-damaged skin with gray-blue granules/peppering, annular-granular structures, regression areas and fragmented patches, suggestive of lentigo maligna/melanoma in situ.

Asymmetric oval lesion with multiple colors (light and dark brown, red, central blue-violet), irregular dots and globules, a central blue-white veil-like area with white scar-like structures, and peripheral erythema with dotted vessels.

Light-to-medium brown lesion with irregular, somewhat asymmetric outline and patchy pigmentation, but colors are limited to tan/brown with a faint reticular pattern and no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels, favoring a dysplastic/benign nevus.

Asymmetric, multilobulated lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (light and dark brown, blue-gray, pink), and irregular pigment blotches with regression-like whitish-pink areas in the center, partly obscured by dense hair.
Irregular asymmetric brown lesion with a central blue-gray veil/regression area, uneven pigment distribution, and irregular borders on background of sun-damaged skin with lentigines.

Asymmetric brown lesion with an eccentric dark purple-brown blotch, irregular peripheral dots and globules, and whitish regression-like areas, which together raise concern for melanoma over a dysplastic nevus.

Asymmetric brown lesion with irregular, fuzzy borders, uneven pigment distribution with darker eccentric blotches, peripheral granular/peppered dots, and a faint irregular light-brown extension, raising concern for melanoma.

A large, poorly defined pink lesion with faint, irregular light-brown reticular and blotchy pigment, polymorphous linear serpentine vessels and whitish regression-like areas raises concern for a hypomelanotic melanoma, though the call is uncertain.
Small light-brown lesion with a fairly uniform faint reticular network, mild border irregularity and slight asymmetry, but no blue-white veil, atypical dots or regression, favoring a benign nevus.

Small elongated lesion with a regular fine pigment network, a darker reddish-brown upper portion fading into lighter tan structureless areas, and no blue-white veil, atypical dots, or regression, favoring a benign nevus (lentiginous/dysplastic type), though the asymmetry warrants some caution.

Asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (dark brown, light brown, pink-white), irregular dark dots/globules and short streaks, regression-like whitish areas, and an irregular, fading network at the periphery.

A small but asymmetric brown lesion on sun-damaged skin, with irregular, ill-defined borders, an eccentric dark blotch with gray dots, and a central whitish regression-like area, which together raise concern for early melanoma or melanoma in situ.

Small light-brown macule with an irregular, notched outline and a slightly darker centre bearing a few fine dots, but colour stays uniform tan-brown with no blue-white veil, atypical network or regression, which favours a benign nevus despite the asymmetry.

Large, asymmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with irregular, fragmented blotches, regression-like white scar areas, pinkish erythema, and irregular linear vessels, suggestive of melanoma in situ or lentigo maligna on sun-damaged skin.
Asymmetric lesion with an eccentric dark black-blue blotch, blue-white veil-like areas, and an atypical, irregular pigment network fading unevenly at the periphery.

A faint, asymmetric, poorly defined light-brown pigmented area with irregular blotches, scar-like whitish regression zones and fine irregular linear vessels on shaved, sun-damaged skin raises concern for a hypomelanotic or in-situ melanoma.

Asymmetric, irregularly shaped brown lesion with an atypical, irregular network, eccentric dark blotches and irregular dots/globules, plus peppering and multifocal hyperpigmentation, suggesting melanoma (likely in situ) over a dysplastic nevus.

Light brown lesion with a fairly uniform, delicate reticular/dotted pattern, a single tan color, and a pinkish fading periphery, though the outline is irregular and asymmetric, most consistent with a benign nevus.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular notched borders, a separate satellite-like fragment, eccentric dark blotch, uneven brown pigmentation, and a bluish-gray regression-like area.

Large ill-defined lesion on sun-damaged skin with asymmetric light-to-dark brown pigmentation, irregular dark granules and dots, regression-like white-pink areas, and angulated lines suggesting lentigo maligna/in situ melanoma.

An asymmetric, irregular lesion on sun-damaged freckled skin shows multiple colors (tan, brown granular/peppered areas and a central pink-red, regression-like zone) with uneven pigment distribution, which favors early melanoma, though a lichen planus-like keratosis is a reasonable alternative.
Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (brown, red, blue-gray), blue-white veil-like areas, peppering/irregular dots and globules, regression structures, and atypical vessels.

Ill-defined, irregular light-brown pigmentation with asymmetric darker brown dots and granules, perifollicular involvement, and a background of erythema with fine linear and dotted vessels on what appears to be sun-damaged facial or scalp skin, raising concern for lentigo maligna or lentigo maligna melanoma.

A pink, largely featureless lesion on sun-damaged skin shows polymorphous linear-irregular and serpentine vessels with a few scattered brown dots and no clear arborizing pattern, which raises concern for amelanotic melanoma.

Nail-unit lesion with destruction of the nail plate, a pink-red ulcerated or amelanotic nodular area, and irregular brown pigment spreading onto the periungual skin (Hutchinson-like sign), all suggesting acral or subungual melanoma.

Small light-to-medium brown lesion with a slightly irregular outline and a few darker clumps, but limited colors, no blue-white veil, and no atypical network on sun-damaged skin favor a benign nevus or solar lentigo, though the asymmetric dark clumping keeps some suspicion.

The lesion is markedly asymmetric with an irregular, notched border, an off-center dark blotch, multiple brown shades, and a whitish-gray regression-like area with fragmented pigment on the left side.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular pigment distribution, an eccentric dark brown area on the right, light-brown structureless zones, and blurred irregular borders favor early melanoma over a nevus.

Facial-type sun-damaged skin with irregular, asymmetric brown-gray pigmentation, a focal blue-gray area, angulated and rhomboidal structures around follicles, and a poorly defined border, all suggesting lentigo maligna.

Small, fairly symmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with a mostly regular outline and homogeneous-to-reticular pigment, though there is mild central color variation and a faint pale area, with no blue-white veil, atypical network or irregular streaks, which favors a benign nevus.
Eccentric blue-gray structureless area with blue-white veil, asymmetric multicomponent coloration (blue, red-brown, pink), irregular blurred borders, and dotted vessels on a pink background.

Small light-to-medium brown macule with fairly uniform tan-brown pigmentation, a slightly darker center, blurred but not abrupt borders, and no atypical network, regression structures, blue-white veil or atypical vessels, though the mild asymmetry and irregular outline including a small inferior projection keep melanoma from being excluded.

Small, fairly symmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with a homogeneous center and a regular rim of peripheral brown dots/globules, consistent with a growing (Clark/Reed-type) nevus rather than melanoma, though the peripheral globules warrant monitoring.

An asymmetric, irregularly bordered pigmented lesion on sun-damaged skin, with several shades of brown, a darker eccentric center, grayish areas and an irregular notched outline, which raises concern for lentigo maligna or melanoma.

Large lesion extending beyond the field, with multiple colors (brown, dark brown, red-brown and blue-gray veil-like zones), an irregular atypical network and blotches at the periphery, and asymmetric structure; the surface keratin and crusting raise seborrheic keratosis as a differential but do not explain the blue-gray areas.

Small light-brown oval lesion with a fairly regular reticular network that fades evenly at the edges, uniform color, and no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical dots, consistent with a benign nevus.

Asymmetric light-to-dark brown lesion with irregular, blurred borders, an atypical network, central blue-gray peppering (granularity), and whitish regression-like areas suggest melanoma, though a regressing nevus cannot be excluded.

Markedly asymmetric, irregular stellate shape with multiple brown, dark brown and blue-gray colors, irregular peripheral projections/streaks, central white regression-like structures, and a surrounding depigmented halo with vessels.

Asymmetric multicomponent lesion with an atypical irregular network, eccentric blue-black blotch, peppering/regression with blue-gray granules, white scar-like areas, and irregular borders on sun-damaged skin.

Small, roughly symmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with a fine regular reticular network fading at the periphery, central hypopigmented dot, and no blue-white veil, atypical dots, or irregular streaks, most consistent with a benign nevus.

A fairly symmetric oval light-to-medium brown lesion with a faint reticular network fading at the edges, a central hypopigmented area and slight pinkish-violet tint, and no atypical network, streaks or blue-white veil, which favors a benign (possibly dysplastic) nevus.

Asymmetric lesion with blue-gray veil, eccentric brown blotch, ulceration/crusts, and irregular polymorphous vessels on a pink background, worrisome for melanoma (basal cell carcinoma is a differential).

Large asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (light-to-dark brown, blue-gray areas), irregular atypical network with eccentric dark blotches, and regression-like whitish/pink zones.

The lesion is asymmetric with ill-defined borders on sun-damaged skin, showing eccentric irregular brown blotches, pinkish regression-like structureless areas with fine dotted or linear vessels, and patchy, uneven pigmentation.

Large, markedly asymmetric multicomponent lesion with an eccentric dark-brown zone of atypical network and irregular peripheral projections, plus a paler area with fine granularity and whitish regression-like zones.

Marked asymmetry with an eccentric dark brown-purple area showing irregular streaks/pseudopods at the periphery, atypical network, blue-gray hue, and a central regression-like pale area separating it from a lighter brown component.

About 8-10 mm lesion with a bilobed, mildly asymmetric outline but fairly uniform light-to-medium brown pigment, a regular reticular/globular pattern and no blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels, which favors a benign nevus, though the asymmetry keeps melanoma risk moderate.

Fairly symmetric oval brown lesion with central darker irregular blotches and slightly blurred, faded periphery, but no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels, favoring a dysplastic or Clark nevus over melanoma.
Small, symmetric oval lesion with uniform dark brown color, a regular fine peripheral rim, and sharp borders, with no regression, blue-white veil, or atypical network, consistent with a benign nevus.
A small asymmetric lesion on sun-damaged, freckled skin shows several colors (light brown, dark brown, eccentric blue-gray), irregular dots and globules, and an uneven, blurred border.

Several small light-to-mid brown islands with moth-eaten borders, milia-like/comedo-like openings and fine peppered dots on sun-damaged skin favor solar lentigo or early seborrheic keratosis, though the fragmented, asymmetric pigment leaves some concern for melanoma.
